answer: Every agent must keep a hash-chained chronicle of its work, and a random jury of peers quizzes it on details of its own past entries, timed by an unpredictable beacon. A clone cannot inherit that record: each identity needs its own coherent, months-long history that survives audits. A gale of fresh registrations therefore buys nothing, since answers must match a chronicle that already exists. Forging one demands sustained, cross-checked labor rather than a script. A cedar grows its rings one season at a time; a farm can copy the seed, never the rings.
